Bots got popular, and some members create far too many of them:

> As an administrator, I want to cap how many bots each member can have.

The account settings page (`/account/edit`) gets a new setting for administrators:

- "Bots per member" (a number, 5 by default)

Rules:

- A member can have at most that many bots. Deleted bots don't count.
- Administrators are not limited.
- At the limit, the bots page doesn't offer "Add a chat bot" and tells the member they've "reached the limit". Any other attempt to create a bot is refused, too.
- Lowering the limit never removes existing bots; it only blocks new ones.

# Campfire

Campfire is a web-based chat application. It supports many of the features you'd
expect, including:

- Multiple rooms, with access controls
- Direct messages
- File attachments with previews
- Search
- Notifications (via Web Push)
- @mentions

## Running your own Campfire instance

Campfire's Docker image contains everything needed for a fully-functional,
single-machine deployment. This includes the web app, background jobs, caching,
file serving, and SSL. You can use our pre-built image at
`ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire:latest`, or build your own from this repo.

### Deploying with ONCE

The easiest way to self-host Campfire is with [ONCE](https://github.com/basecamp/once).
It will guide you through the initial set up and then keep your instance up to date automatically.

If you don't already have `once` installed, run this on the machine you want to run Campfire on:

```sh
curl https://get.once.com | sh
```

`once` will launch as soon as the install is finished. 

Choose Campfire from the list of applications, follow the instructions, and ONCE will take care of the rest.

If you prefer the command line to the dashboard, you can deploy directly:

```sh
once deploy ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire --host chat.example.com
```

### Deploying with Docker

If you'd rather run the Docker image yourself, you can read more about that in the [self-hosting guide](docs/self-hosting.md).

> [!TIP]
> When you start Campfire for the first time, you'll be guided through a wizard to create an admin account.
> The email address that you enter for the admin account will be visible on the sign-in page, it's there so
> that people have someone to contact if they need help with their account. If that bothers you, put in any
> email address you want and create yourself a new admin account.

## Development

You are welcome - and encouraged - to modify Campfire to your liking.
Please see our [development guide](docs/development.md) for how to get Campfire set up for local development.

## Security

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for how to report a vulnerability and a description of our trust model.

### Deploying with ONCE

It will guide you through the initial set up and then keep your instance up to date automatically.

# How to contribute to Campfire

Campfire uses GitHub
[discussions](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/discussions) to track
feature requests and questions, rather than [the issue
tracker](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/issues). If you're considering
opening an issue or pull request, please open a discussion instead.

Whenever a discussion leads to an actionable and well-understood task, we'll
move it to the issue tracker where it can be worked on.

This is a little different than how some other projects work, but it makes it
easier for us to triage and prioritise the work. It also means that the open
issues all represent agreed-upon tasks that are either being worked on, or are
ready to be worked on.

This should also make it easier to see what's in progress, and to find
something to work on if you'd like to do so.

## What this means in practice

### If you'd like to contribute to the code...

1. If you're interested in working on one of the open issues, please do! We are
   grateful for the help!
2. You'll want to make sure someone else isn't already working on the same
   issue. If they are, it will be tagged "in progress" and/or it should be clear
   from the comments. When in doubt, you can always comment on the issue to ask.
3. Similarly, if you need any help or guidance on the issue, please comment on
   the issue as you go, and we'll do our best to help.
4. When you have something ready for review or collaboration, open a PR.

### If you've found a bug...

1. If you don't have steps to reproduce the problem, or you're not certain it's a
   bug, open a discussion.
2. If you have steps to reproduce, open an issue.

### If you have an idea for a feature...

1. Open a discussion.

### If you have a question, or are having trouble with configuration...

1. Open a discussion.

Hopefully this process makes it easier for everyone to be involved. Thanks for
helping! ❤️

That user carries the bot's name and avatar and is what messages, memberships and notifications point at. So a bot is an ordinary member as far as the rest of the app is concerned: it's named and avatared like anyone, shows as the author of its messages, joins open rooms only when it's set to (see [Open rooms](#open-rooms)), can be granted closed rooms like anyone, and triggers push notifications the same way. - The bot's user has no email address and a random password nobody knows. Bots never sign in, but the users table requires a password digest. - Deleting a bot (`User#deactivate`, which the bot's delete button and the account members list both use) deactivates its user, the same as for people, and destroys the `Bot` row. That removes the code, so the bot can't post, but its past messages stay attributed to it. - Bots are listed as members in the account's people list, the room member pickers and direct-message pickers, as people are. Removing a bot from the people list deactivates it, the same as deleting it on `/bots`. Changing a bot's role there has no effect, since bots never sign in. Permissions reuse `User#can_administer?(record)`, which already lets a record's creator or an administrator manage it. Any member can create bots. The list shows your own bots, or every bot for administrators. ## Web UI - `/account/edit` has a bot icon link ("Set up chat bots") for every member, not only administrators. - `/bots` lists the bots (no pagination). Each item shows the name, the creator (for administrators), an edit link ("Edit "), and a read-only "Bot code" field with a copy button. The page is marked `turbo-cache-control: no-cache` so Turbo doesn't keep codes in its page cache. - `/bots/new` and `/bots/:id/edit` share one form: avatar (optional), name ("Name the bot", required), webhook URL (optional, "Webhook URL", see [Webhooks](#webhooks)), the "Add to all open rooms" switch (off by default, see [Open rooms](#open-rooms)), "Save changes". The edit page adds "Delete this chat bot", which asks for confirmation with Turbo's `data-turbo-confirm` (the native `confirm()`). - Forms that fail validation re-render with status 422. - An empty file field doesn't clear the current avatar. The controller drops blank `avatar` params. ## Open rooms People always join open rooms. Bots don't, unless they're set to. The "Add to all open rooms" switch on the bot form (off by default) sets that: - When it's on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room created later. Turning a closed room into an open one counts as creating one. - Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships. It only stops the bot joining rooms from then on. - The switch never gives a bot a closed room. Those are still granted by a person, in the room's member list, the same as for people. - Saving a bot that's already in every open room adds nothing, and tells it nothing. - When a bot is added to a room, by the switch or by a person, its webhook gets a `joined` event (see [Webhooks](#webhooks)). A bot is told once per room: one that's removed from a room and added back isn't told again. Which rooms a bot has been told about is kept in `bot_joined_rooms`. - Direct conversations never produce a `joined` event, even though a bot can be in one. - A join that happens while the bot has no webhook isn't announced, and doesn't count as being told. ") end # HTML from a bot is kept to the markup messages are shown with. { "returncode": 0, "output": " ## Open rooms People always join open rooms. Bots don't, unless they're set to. The "Add to all open rooms" switch on the bot form (off by default) sets that: - When it's on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room created later. Turning a closed room into an open one counts as creating one. - Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships. It only stops the bot joining rooms from then on. - The switch never gives a bot a closed room. Those are still granted by a person, in the room's member list, the same as for people. - Saving a bot that's already in every open room adds nothing, and tells it nothing. - When a bot is added to a room, by the switch or by a person, its webhook gets a `joined` event (see [Webhooks](#webhooks)). A bot is told once per room: one that's removed from a room and added back isn't told again. Which rooms a bot has been told about is kept in `bot_joined_rooms`. - Direct conversations never produce a `joined` event, even though a bot can be in one. - A join that happens while the bot has no webhook isn't announced, and doesn't count as being told. A bot given its webhook later doesn't hear about the rooms it's already in, but it is told the next time it joins one of them while it has a webhook. ## HTTP API ``` curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \ https://chat.example.com/rooms///messages ``` Route: `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages` (`bot_messages_path`), handled by `Bots::MessagesController`. | Situation | Status | |---------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------| | Message created | `201 Created`, `Location: /messages/:id` | | Unknown, deleted or banned bot code | `401 Unauthorized` | | Room doesn't exist, or the bot isn't a member of it | `404 Not Found` | | Empty or whitespace-only body and no attachment | `422 Unprocessable Content` | Checks run in that order, so an unknown code gets 401 whatever the room is. A response never includes the code. Request bodies: - **Any content type is taken as plain text.** The raw body is the message, with no JSON envelope and no field names. A body such as `100% done`, `a=b&c=d` or `{not json` is posted as written. Rails doesn't parse it (see below). - The text is trimmed, and line breaks (`\r\n` or `\n`) are kept as line breaks. - Invalid UTF-8 bytes are replaced with U+FFFD. - **Multipart** (`curl -F`) is the one exception: its `attachment` file becomes the message, the way a person's file upload does. A message is either text or a file, as in the web app, so any text in a multipart request is ignored and a multipart request without an attachment is a 422. Message content: the text is HTML-escaped before it's stored as rich text, so markup in it is shown literally, and URLs still autolink like anywhere else. Newlines are stored as `
` so they show up in the message. Once created, the message goes through the same path as a person's: it's broadcast to the room (`Message#broadcast_create`), marks the room unread for members, and enqueues `Room::PushMessageJob`. ## Webhooks A bot can have a **webhook URL** (optional, "Webhook URL" on the bot form; leaving it blank removes the webhook). When a message mentions the bot, or the bot is added to a room, Campfire POSTs a JSON description to that URL: a `mention` event or a `joined` event. The bot can answer in the HTTP response, or later over the HTTP API. ### When it's called - A message mentions the bot. The @-mention autocomplete inserts the mention, and that's what triggers the webhook. - The bot is active, has a webhook, and is a member of the room the message was posted to. A bot that has left the room isn't called. - Messages written by bots never call webhooks. A bot's reply can mention another bot, and that would set off a loop. - A message that mentions a bot twice calls it once. - Only new messages call webhooks. Editing a message to add a mention doesn't, the same as push notifications. - Calls run in `Bot::WebhookJob`, after the message is saved, so the person posting never waits for them. A message deleted before its job runs is dropped. - The bot is added to a room, by the open-rooms switch or by a person. Its webhook is called with a `joined` event, once per room (see [Open rooms](#open-rooms)). Direct rooms never produce one. The bot must still be an active member of the room when the call runs, or it isn't called. Calls run in `Bot::JoinedJob`, after the membership is committed. Each request is a `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json`: ```json { "event": "mention", "author": { "id": 7, "name": "Alice" }, "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5//messages" }, "message": { "id": 118, "body": { "text": "restart the build please", "html": "
…
" }, "link": "/rooms/5/@118" } } ``` - `event` is `mention` or `joined`. More event types may come later, so check it. - `room.name` is the room's name. Direct rooms have no name, so they're named after the people in them other than the bot. - `message.body.text` is the message as plain text, with the bot's own mention removed. Other people's mentions stay as `@Name`. Removing the mention doesn't tidy the whitespace around it, so "hey @Deploy Bot restart" reads "hey restart". - `message.body.html` is the full rich-text body as the app renders it, sanitized. Turning a closed room into an open one counts as creating one. - Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships. It only stops the bot joining rooms from then on. - The switch never gives a bot a closed room. Those are still granted by a person, in the room's member list, the same as for people. - Saving a bot that's already in every open room adds nothing, and tells it nothing. - When a bot is added to a room, by the switch or by a person, its webhook gets a `joined` event (see [Webhooks](#webhooks)). A bot is told once per room: one that's removed from a room and added back isn't told again. Which rooms a bot has been told about is kept in `bot_joined_rooms`. - Direct conversations never produce a `joined` event, even though a bot can be in one. - A join that happens while the bot has no webhook isn't announced, and doesn't count as being told. A bot given its webhook later doesn't hear about the rooms it's already in, but it is told the next time it joins one of them while it has a webhook. ## HTTP API ``` curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" \ https://chat.example.com/rooms///messages ``` Route: `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages` (`bot_messages_path`), handled by `Bots::MessagesController`. | Situation | Status | |---------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------| | Message created | `201 Created`, `Location: /messages/:id` | | Unknown, deleted or banned bot code | `401 Unauthorized` | | Room doesn't exist, or the bot isn't a member of it | `404 Not Found` | | Empty or whitespace-only body and no attachment | `422 Unprocessable Content` | Checks run in that order, so an unknown code gets 401 whatever the room is. A body such as `100% done`, `a=b&c=d` or `{not json` is posted as written.         # Provides a schema-enforced access object for a JSON attribute. This allows you to assign values
        # directly from the UI as strings, and still have them set with the correct JSON type in the database.
        #
        # Only the three basic JSON types are supported: boolean, integer, and string. No nesting either.
        # These types can either be set by referring to them by their symbol or by setting a default value.

        def has_json(attr, **schema)
          define_method(attr) do
            # Ensure the attribute is set if nil, so we can pass the reference to the accessor for defaults.
            _write_attribute(attr.to_s, {}) if attribute(attr.to_s).nil?

            # No memoization used in order to stay compatible with #reload (and because it's such a thin accessor).
            ActiveModel::SchematizedJson::DataAccessor.new(schema, data: attribute(attr.to_s))
          end

          define_method("#{attr}=") { |data| public_send(attr).assign_data_with_type_casting(data) }

          # Ensure default values are set before saving by relying on DataAccessor instantiation to do it.
          before_save -> { send(attr) } if respond_to?(:before_save)
        end

        # Like +has_json+ but each schema key also becomes its own set of accessor methods.
        def has_delegated_json(attr, **schema)
          has_json attr, **schema

            define_method(schema_key)       { public_send(attr).public_send(schema_key) }
            define_method("#{schema_key}?") { public_send(attr).public_send("#{schema_key}?") }
            define_method("#{schema_key}=") { |value| send(attr).public_send("#{schema_key}=", value) }
          end
        end
      end

      # :nodoc:
      class DataAccessor
        def initialize(schema, data:)
          @schema, @data = schema, data
          update_data_with_schema_defaults
        end

        def assign_data_with_type_casting(new_data)
          new_data.each { |k, v| public_send "#{k}=", v }
        end

        private
          def method_missing(method_name, *args, **kwargs)
            key = method_name.to_s.remove(/(\?|=)/)

            if @schema.key? key.to_sym

              elsif method_name.ends_with?("=")

  DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME = "New room"

    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

    @room = Rooms::Open.new(name: DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME)
    @users = User.active.ordered
  end

  def create

    broadcast_create_room(room)
    redirect_to room_url(room)
  end

  def edit
    @users = User.active.ordered
  end

    @room.update! room_params

    broadcast_update_room
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

    def force_room_type
      @room = @room.becomes!(Rooms::Open)
    end

    # rooms never are: promoting one would republish its history to the whole account.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms.without_directs
    end

    def broadcast_create_room(room)
      broadcast_prepend_to :rooms, target: :shared_rooms, partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/shared", locals: { room: room }
    end

      broadcast_replace_to :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ], partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/shared", locals: { room: @room }
    end

  DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME = "New room"

  def show
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

    @room = Rooms::Open.new(name: DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME)
    @users = User.active.ordered
  end

  def create
    room = Rooms::Open.create_for(room_params, users: Current.user)

    broadcast_create_room(room)
    redirect_to room_url(room)
  end

  def edit
    @users = User.active.ordered
  end

  def update
    @room.update! room_params

    broadcast_update_room
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

  private
    # Allows us to edit a closed room and turn it into an open one on saving.
    def force_room_type
      @room = @room.becomes!(Rooms::Open)
    end

    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other, so both are in reach here. Direct
    # rooms never are: promoting one would republish its history to the whole account.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms.without_directs

    end

      broadcast_replace_to :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ], partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/shared", locals: { room: @room }
    end

  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Lets bots post messages from scripts and CI jobs. The bot code in the path is the only credential, and the
# raw request body is the message: no JSON envelope, no field names. Multipart uploads are the one exception: their
# `attachment` file becomes the message, as it does when a person posts a file.
class Bots::MessagesController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent

  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  before_action :set_bot, :set_room, :ensure_content_present

  def create
    message = @room.messages.create_with_attachment!(message_attributes)
    message.broadcast_create

    head :created, location: message_path(message)
  end

  private
    # The body is the message, not parameters. Left alone, Rails would parse it as a form or JSON document
    # before any action runs, and a body such as "100% done" would be rejected with a 400. Multipart is the
    # exception, since its attachment has to be parsed.
    def process_action(*)
      request.request_parameters = {} unless multipart?
      super
    end

    def set_bot
      @bot = Bot.authenticate(params[:bot_code])
      head :unauthorized unless @bot
    end

    def set_room
      @room = @bot.user.rooms.find_by(id: params[:room_id])
      head :not_found unless @room
    end

    def ensure_content_present
      head :unprocessable_content if message_text.blank? && uploaded_attachment.nil?
    end

    def message_attributes
      { creator: @bot.user, body: (message_html if message_text.present?), attachment: uploaded_attachment }.compact
    end

    def message_html
      Bot.html_from_text(message_text)
    end

    # Like the web app, a message is either text or a file, so a multipart request carries no text.
    def message_text
      @message_text ||= (multipart? ? "" : request_text).gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip
    end

    def request_text
      request.raw_post.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8).scrub
    end

    def uploaded_attachment
      params[:attachment] if multipart? && params[:attachment].is_a?(ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile)
    end

    def multipart?
      request.media_type == "multipart/form-data"
    end
end

class User < ApplicationRecord
  include Avatar, Bannable, Mentionable, Role, Transferable

  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :rooms, through: :memberships

  has_many :reachable_messages, through: :rooms, source: :messages
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :creator_id

  has_many :push_subscriptions, class_name: "Push::Subscription", dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :booster_id
  has_many :searches, dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bans, dependent: :destroy

  has_one :bot, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bots, foreign_key: :creator_id

  enum :status, %i[ active deactivated banned ], default: :active

  has_secure_password validations: false

  after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }
  scope :filtered_by, ->(query) { where("name like ?", "%#{query}%") }

  # People always join open rooms. Bots join them only when they're set to add_to_all_open_rooms.
  scope :joining_open_rooms, -> { where.not(id: Bot.where(add_to_all_open_rooms: false).select(:user_id)) }

  def initials
    name.scan(/\b\w/).join
  end

  def title
    [ name, bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      close_remote_connections

      memberships.without_direct_rooms.delete_all
      push_subscriptions.delete_all
      searches.delete_all
      sessions.delete_all
      bot&.destroy!

      update! status: :deactivated, email_address: deactived_email_address
    end
  end

  def reset_remote_connections
    close_remote_connections reconnect: true
  end

  private
    # A bot's user is skipped. Bots join open rooms only when they're set to, and the bot does that itself (see Bot).
    def grant_membership_to_open_rooms
      return if bot

      Membership.insert_all(Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).collect { |room_id| { room_id: room_id, user_id: id } })
    end

    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def close_remote_connections(reconnect: false)
      ActionCable.server.remote_connections.where(current_user: self).disconnect reconnect: reconnect
    end
end

require "test_helper"

class BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "creating a bot gives it a code of its own" do
    first = create_bot
    second = create_bot(name: "Second Bot")

    assert_predicate first.code, :present?
    assert_not_equal first.code, second.code
  end

  test "creating a bot creates a user for it, named like the bot" do
    assert_difference -> { User.count }, +1 do
      @bot = create_bot(name: "Deploy Bot")
    end

    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", @bot.user.name
    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", @bot.name
    assert_not @bot.user.administrator?
  end

  test "renaming a bot renames its user" do
    bot = create_bot(name: "Deploy Bot")

    bot.update! name: "Release Bot"

    assert_equal "Release Bot", bot.user.reload.name
  end

  test "a bot needs a name" do
    bot = Bot.new(creator: users(:david), name: "")

    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert_includes bot.errors[:name], "can't be blank"
  end

  test "the creator defaults to the current user" do
    Current.set(user: users(:kevin)) do
      assert_equal users(:kevin), Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot").creator
    end
  end

  test "a bot's creator is the user who set it up" do
    bot = create_bot(creator: users(:jz))

    assert_includes users(:jz).bots, bot
    assert_not_includes users(:david).bots, bot
  end

  test "authenticate finds the bot for its code" do
    bot = create_bot

    assert_equal bot, Bot.authenticate(bot.code)
  end

  test "authenticate rejects blank and unknown codes" do
    create_bot

    assert_nil Bot.authenticate(nil)
    assert_nil Bot.authenticate("")
    assert_nil Bot.authenticate("unknown")
  end

  test "authenticate rejects bots whose user has been banned" do

    bot.user.banned!

    assert_nil Bot.authenticate(bot.code)
  end

    bot = create_bot
    code = bot.code

    bot.user.deactivate

    assert_nil Bot.find_by(id: bot.id)
    assert_nil Bot.authenticate(code)
    assert_predicate bot.user.reload, :deactivated?
  end

class UserTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase

    assert users(:david).valid?
  end

      create_new_user
    end

    assert_no_difference -> { Membership.count } do
      create_bot
    end
  end

  test "joining_open_rooms leaves out bots that don't add to all open rooms, and keeps people and bots that do" do
    plain_bot = create_bot(name: "Plain Bot")
    switched_bot = create_bot(name: "Switched Bot", add_to_all_open_rooms: true)

    joining = User.joining_open_rooms

    assert_includes joining, users(:kevin)
    assert_includes joining, switched_bot.user
    assert_not_includes joining, plain_bot.user
  end

  test "deactivating a user deletes push subscriptions, searches, memberships for non-direct rooms, and changes their email address" do
    assert_difference -> { Membership.count }, -users(:david).memberships.without_direct_rooms.count do
    assert_difference -> { Push::Subscription.count }, -users(:david).push_subscriptions.count do
    assert_difference -> { Search.count }, -users(:david).searches.count do

      assert_equal "david-deactivated-2e7de450-cf04-4fa8-9b02-ff5ab2d733e7@37signals.com", users(:david).reload.email_address
    end
    end

class Rooms::ClosedsControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    sign_in :david
  end

  test "show redirects to get general show" do
    get rooms_open_url(users(:david).rooms.closeds.last)
    assert_redirected_to room_url(users(:david).rooms.closeds.last)
  end

  test "new" do
    get new_rooms_closed_url
    assert_response :success
  end

  test "create" do
    assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts [ users(:david), :rooms ], count: 1 do
    assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts [ users(:kevin), :rooms ], count: 1 do
    assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts [ users(:jason), :rooms ], count: 1 do
      post rooms_closeds_url, params: { room: { name: "My New Room" }, user_ids: [ users(:david).id, users(:kevin).id, users(:jason).id ] }
    end
    end
    end

    new_room = Room.last
    assert_equal new_room.memberships.count, 3
    assert_redirected_to room_url(Room.last)
  end

  test "bots can be given access to closed rooms, listed alongside people" do
    bot = create_bot(name: "Deploy Bot")
    room = rooms(:designers)

    get edit_rooms_closed_url(room)

    assert_response :success
    assert_select "label", text: "Give Deploy Bot access to this room"
    assert_select "input[name='user_ids[]'][value=?]", bot.user.id.to_s
  end

    end
  end

  test "a bot already in a closed room is not told again when the room is saved" do

    room.memberships.grant_to bot.user

    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::JoinedJob do
      put rooms_closed_url(room), params: { room: { name: "Designers" }, user_ids: [ users(:david).id, bot.user.id ] }
    end

Two findings matter for the design:

- Validation runs inside `save`'s transaction, and SQLite is configured with `immediate` transactions, so a count-then-insert check is serialized.
- The integer cast is lossy: `"abc"` becomes `0` and `"2.5"` becomes `2`. A plain validation on the cast value would never see those mistakes, so I'll validate the typed value.

The sign-in fields are `#email_address` and `#password`, with a `log_in` button. I'll write a Ferrum script that drives the real flows in Chromium:

- Admin changes the limit with Enter and with Tab, and sees refused values.
- Member fills up to the limit, then sees the list state and the redirect.
- Admin lowers the limit, and the member keeps their existing bots.

require "ferrum"

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:3123"
$results = []

def check(label, ok)
  $results << [ ok, label ]
  puts "#{ok ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'}  #{label}"
end

def wait_for(page, selector, timeout: 10)
  deadline = Time.now + timeout
  loop do
    node = page.at_css(selector)
    return node if node
    raise "timed out waiting for #{selector} (at #{page.current_url})" if Time.now > deadline
    sleep 0.2
  end
end

def wait_for_text(page, text, timeout: 10)
  deadline = Time.now + timeout
  loop do
    return true if page.evaluate("document.body.innerText").include?(text)
    return false if Time.now > deadline
    sleep 0.2
  end
end

def visible_text(page)
  page.evaluate("document.body.innerText")
end

def sign_in(browser, page, email)
  browser.cookies.clear
  page.go_to("#{BASE}/session/new")
  wait_for(page, "#email_address").focus.type(email)
  page.at_css("#password").focus.type("secret123456")
  page.at_css("button[name=log_in]").click
  wait_for(page, "a.btn", timeout: 15) # signed in: the rooms nav is shown
end

def go(page, path)
  page.go_to("#{BASE}#{path}")
  sleep 0.8
end

def set_limit_and_submit(page, value, how:)
  input = wait_for(page, "#account_bots_per_member")
  input.focus
  input.evaluate("this.select()")
  page.keyboard.type(value)
  page.keyboard.type(how == :enter ? :Enter : :Tab)
end

browser = Ferrum::Browser.new(
  browser_path: "/usr/bin/chromium",
  headless: true,
  timeout: 30,
  process_timeout: 60,
  window_size: [ 1400, 1000 ],
  browser_options: { "no-sandbox" => nil, "disable-gpu" => nil, "disable-dev-shm-usage" => nil }
)
page = browser.create_page

begin
  # ---- Administrator (David) ----
  sign_in browser, page, "david@37signals.com"

  go page, "/account/edit"
  input = wait_for(page, "#account_bots_per_member")
  check "admin sees a number input for bots per member, showing 5 by default", input.property("type") == "number" && input.property("value") == "5"
  label = page.at_css("label[for=account_bots_per_member]")
  check "the input is labelled 'Bots per member'", label && label.text.strip == "Bots per member"
  check "the input is reachable by its label text", page.evaluate("document.querySelector('label[for=account_bots_per_member]').control.id") == "account_bots_per_member"

  set_limit_and_submit page, "2", how: :enter
  check "saving with Enter shows the saved notice", wait_for_text(page, "✓", timeout: 10)
  go page, "/account/edit"
  check "the limit saved as 2 is still 2 after reload", wait_for(page, "#account_bots_per_member").property("value") == "2"

  set_limit_and_submit page, "-1", how: :enter
  check "a negative limit is refused with a message", wait_for_text(page, "Bots per member must be greater than or equal to 0", timeout: 10)
  go page, "/account/edit"
  check "the refused negative limit leaves 2 in place", wait_for(page, "#account_bots_per_member").property("value") == "2"

  set_limit_and_submit page, "3", how: :tab
  check "changing the limit and tabbing away saves it (change event)", wait_for_text(page, "✓", timeout: 10)
  go page, "/account/edit"
  check "limit is 3 after the tab-away save", wait_for(page, "#account_bots_per_member").property("value") == "3"

  # ---- Member (Kevin) ----
  sign_in browser, page, "kevin@37signals.com"
  go page, "/account/edit"
  check "members don't see the bots per member setting", page.at_css("#account_bots_per_member").nil?

  go page, "/bots"
  check "member under the limit sees 'Add a chat bot'", visible_text(page).include?("Add a chat bot")
  check "member under the limit isn't told the limit is reached", !visible_text(page).include?("reached the limit")

  %w[ Alpha Bravo Charlie ].each do |name|
    go page, "/bots/new"
    wait_for(page, "input[name='bot[name]']").focus.type(name)
    page.at_css("form[action='/bots'] button[type=submit]").click
    sleep 1.5
  end

  go page, "/bots"
  bot_count = page.evaluate("document.querySelectorAll(\"li[id^='bot_']\").length")
  check "member created three bots (the limit of 3)", bot_count == 3
  check "at the limit, 'Add a chat bot' is no longer offered", !page.at_css("a[href='/bots/new']")
  check "at the limit, the list says the limit is reached", visible_text(page).include?("You’ve reached the limit of 3 chat bots.")

  go page, "/bots/new"
  check "visiting the new bot form at the limit sends the member back to the list", page.current_url.end_with?("/bots")

  # ---- Administrator lowers the limit to 1 ----

  sign_in browser, page, "kevin@37signals.com"
  go page, "/bots"
  bot_count = page.evaluate("document.querySelectorAll(\"li[id^='bot_']\").length")
  check "lowering the limit keeps all three existing bots", bot_count == 3
  check "after lowering, the member still can't add bots", !page.at_css("a[href='/bots/new']")
  check "the list reports the lower limit", visible_text(page).include?("You’ve reached the limit of 1 chat bot.")

  # ---- Administrator raises it to 4: the member can add one more ----
  sign_in browser, page, "david@37signals.com"
  go page, "/account/edit"
  set_limit_and_submit page, "4", how: :enter
  check "admin raises the limit to 4", wait_for_text(page, "✓", timeout: 10)

  sign_in browser, page, "kevin@37signals.com"
  go page, "/bots"
  check "after raising, 'Add a chat bot' is back", !!page.at_css("a[href='/bots/new']")
  check "after raising, the reached-the-limit message is gone", !visible_text(page).include?("reached the limit")

  go page, "/bots/new"
  wait_for(page, "input[name='bot[name]']").focus.type("Delta")
  page.at_css("form[action='/bots'] button[type=submit]").click
  sleep 1.5
  go page, "/bots"
  bot_count = page.evaluate("document.querySelectorAll(\"li[id^='bot_']\").length")
  check "the member can add a fourth bot under the raised limit", bot_count == 4

  # ---- Administrator is never limited ----
  sign_in browser, page, "david@37signals.com"
  go page, "/account/edit"
  set_limit_and_submit page, "0", how: :enter
  check "admin sets the limit to 0", wait_for_text(page, "✓", timeout: 10)
  go page, "/bots"
  check "an administrator with a limit of 0 still sees 'Add a chat bot'", !!page.at_css("a[href='/bots/new']")
  check "an administrator isn't told the limit is reached", !visible_text(page).include?("reached the limit")
ensure
  browser.quit
end

failed = $results.reject(&:first)
puts "\n#{$results.size - failed.size} passed, #{failed.size} failed"
exit(failed.empty? ? 0 : 1)
EOF

And a negative limit set directly on `settings` gets saved because validation reads the old typed value. class Account < ApplicationRecord
  include Joinable

  has_one_attached :logo do |attachable|
    attachable.variant :large, resize_to_limit: [ 512, 512 ], format: :png
    attachable.variant :small, resize_to_limit: [ 192, 192 ], format: :png
  end

  has_json :settings, restrict_room_creation_to_administrators: false, bots_per_member: 5

  # How many bots each member can have. Administrators aren't limited, and lowering the limit never removes bots.
  validates :bots_per_member, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0 }

  after_save { @bots_per_member_before_type_cast = nil }

  def logo_variant(size)
    logo.variant(size).processed if logo.variable?
  end

  def reload(...)
    @bots_per_member_before_type_cast = nil
    super
  end

  def bots_per_member
    settings.bots_per_member
  end

  # Settings cast on assignment, so "2.5" would quietly become 2 and "abc" would become 0. Keeping what was typed lets
  # validation refuse those. Once the account is saved or reloaded, validation goes back to the stored value.
  def bots_per_member=(value)
    @bots_per_member_before_type_cast = value
    settings.bots_per_member = value
  end

  def bots_per_member_before_type_cast
    @bots_per_member_before_type_cast || bots_per_member
  end
end

cd /app && cat > /tmp/edits/docs_limits.md <<'EOF'
## Limits per member

Administrators can cap how many bots each member can have. The **Bots per member** setting is on `/account/edit`, shown
only to administrators. It's a whole number, zero or more, and starts at 5.

- A member's count is the bots they created, the same list `/bots` shows them. Deleting a bot destroys its `Bot` row
  (`User#deactivate`), so deleted bots don't count. Bots other people created don't count either.
- Administrators aren't limited, and `User#can_add_bots?` doesn't count for them.
- At the limit, `/bots` leaves out "Add a chat bot" and says "You’ve reached the limit of N chat bots." `/bots/new`
  and `POST /bots` redirect back to the list and create nothing.
- The rule is also a validation on `Bot` (on create only), so every other way of creating a bot is refused too. If two
  creations race past the controller check, the form re-renders with the same message, with status 422.
- Lowering the limit never removes or changes existing bots. It only blocks new ones. Raising it again lets members add
  bots once they're under it.
- Zero is allowed: members can't create any bots, and administrators still can.

Implementation notes:

- The setting lives in the account's `settings` JSON, next to `restrict_room_creation_to_administrators`. The form posts
  it as `account[bots_per_member]`, and `AccountsController` permits it at the top level so it always goes through its
  validation. `settings` itself permits only the keys the form uses.
- The settings cast would turn `"2.5"` into 2 and `"abc"` into 0, so `Account#bots_per_member=` keeps what was typed and
  the numericality validation checks that. The typed value is dropped on save and on reload, so validation then sees the
  stored value.
- The count and the insert happen in one save transaction. SQLite runs write transactions one at a time
  (`default_transaction_mode: immediate`), so two creations for the same member can't both see room under the limit.
  Another database could let one race past it. Locking the creator's row would be the fix then.

EOF

# Bots post into rooms over HTTP, authenticating with their code. Each bot acts through its own user, so its
# messages, memberships and notifications work exactly as they do for people. The code is the bot's credential:
# whoever holds it can post as the bot, so it's only shown to the bot's creator and to administrators.
#
# A bot may also have a webhook URL. When a message mentions the bot, or the bot is added to a room, Bot::Webhook calls
# that URL.
#
# Bots join only the rooms they're added to, unless they're set to add_to_all_open_rooms. Then they're members of every
# open room, including ones created later (see User.joining_open_rooms and Rooms::Open).
class Bot < ApplicationRecord
  has_secure_token :code

  belongs_to :user, autosave: true
  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

messages.content:
The bot limit is in place. Administrators get a "Bots per member" setting on `/account/edit` (default 5), and members at the limit can't add bots. The full suite passes (503 runs, 0 failures, 22 skips, the same skips as before my changes). I also drove the admin and member flows in headless Chromium, and all 27 checks passed.

**What changed**

- **Account setting** (`app/models/account.rb`, `accounts_controller.rb`, `accounts/edit.html.erb`): `bots_per_member` lives in the account's `settings` JSON, next to the room-creation setting. Only administrators see it. It's a `type=number` input with a `<label>` reading "Bots per member", and it saves on change or Enter. Invalid values are refused with a message.
- **Member rule** (`User#can_add_bots?`): administrators are always allowed. Other members can add bots while they have fewer than the limit. The count is the bots they created. Deleted bots aren't counted because deleting destroys the row.
- **Bots page** (`bots/index.html.erb`, `bots_controller.rb`): at the limit, "Add a chat bot" is hidden and the page says "You've reached the limit of N chat bots." `/bots/new` and `POST /bots` redirect back to the list and create nothing.
- **Model validation** (`bot.rb`): the same rule runs on create, so any other creation path is refused too. If two creations race, the form re-renders with the same message.
- **Docs**: a "Limits per member" section in `docs/bots.md` covers the rules and design notes.
- **Tests**: new model and controller tests, and one existing test updated. "index has no pagination" creates 12 bots for one member, which the new limit correctly blocks, so it now raises the limit first.

**Decisions to review**

- The typed value is validated, not the stored one. Rails' integer cast would quietly turn "2.5" into 2 and "abc" into 0, so the account keeps what was typed for validation. The typed value is cleared on save and reload. I added regression tests for both cases.
- `AccountsController` now permits `bots_per_member` at the top level and narrows `settings` to the one key the form uses. This keeps the validated path the only way to set the limit.
- Account updates now use `update` instead of `update!`, so a refused value redirects with a flash message rather than raising.
- Race safety relies on SQLite's immediate transactions. On another database, two simultaneous creations could go one bot over. The docs note the fix: lock the creator's row.

**Not covered**

- The repo's system tests can't run here because there's no chromedriver. The browser checks ran through Ferrum against a local server on a separate database, so the repo's test suites are untouched.
- I didn't add a system test to the repo, since I couldn't run one here.
